**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land my whole life. My husband works construction in Shijiazhuang most of the year, so I handle the fields mostly myself, with help from neighbors during busy seasons. We have about 12 mu of contracted land — flat, good loam soil, with access to the village well for irrigation.

I'm not going to try anything new or risky at my age, with just the two of us to rely on. Every family in this village grows winter wheat and summer maize back-to-back. That's what the land is suited for, that's what the grain station buys, and that's what I know how to do. The wheat goes in after autumn, comes out in June, then I turn the ground and get the corn in immediately after. Two harvests, same land.

I'll keep a small strip near the house — about 1 mu — for garlic and vegetables. That's for the family, not to sell.

For seeds, I'll buy the wheat seed the village cooperative recommends — Jimai 22 has been reliable for us, and my neighbor got a good yield last year with it. For corn I always use hybrid — the non-hybrids can't compete anymore.

For fertilizer, I'll do what I always do: base fertilizer before planting, then topdress nitrogen at jointing for the wheat. The soil here isn't rich on its own. I know the agronomist on TV says we use too much urea, but I'd rather not risk a thin crop. I'll irrigate wheat four times — I skip the fourth one only if it rains in May, which it usually doesn't.

The corn I'll manage lighter — one rotary pass after wheat harvest, direct seed, and mostly let the summer rain do the work. I'll irrigate twice if it's dry.
